answer: **Short answer:** Yes, in my understanding. The Central Bank of Ireland permits a UCITS ETF to have both listed (ETF) and unlisted share classes in one fund. I can't confirm the current wording or numbering of Q&A 1088, so check the latest CBI UCITS Q&A. **Prospectus disclosure should compare the classes on:** - **Dealing:** ETF classes deal in the primary market through authorised participants, with others trading on exchange. Unlisted classes deal directly with the fund. - **Settlement:** exchange/CSD cycles versus transfer-agent timetable. - **Costs:** TER, brokerage, spreads, duties or anti-dilution levies. - **Minimums:** creation-unit sizes versus minimum initial and holding amounts. - **Rights:** redemption differences, including direct redemption if the secondary market is disrupted. - **Liquidity:** exchange depth versus dealing frequency. - **Price:** exchange price, which can trade at a premium or discount to NAV, versus dealing at NAV. ESMA ETF guidelines (2014/937) still apply, including the "UCITS ETF"
original_answer:
**Short answer:** Yes, in my understanding. The Central Bank of Ireland permits a UCITS ETF to have both listed (ETF) and unlisted share classes in the same fund. I can't confirm the exact current wording or numbering of Q&A 1088, so check the latest CBI UCITS Q&A document.

**Disclosure the prospectus should make clear (comparison of the classes):**
- **Dealing:** ETF classes deal in the primary market through authorised participants, and other investors trade on exchange. Unlisted classes subscribe and redeem directly with the fund.
- **Settlement:** exchange and CSD settlement cycles versus the transfer-agent settlement timetable.
- **Costs:** TER, brokerage, bid-ask spreads and any duties or anti-dilution levies, which may differ.
- **Minimums:** creation-unit sizes versus minimum initial and holding amounts.
- **Rights:** any differences in redemption access, including direct redemption when the secondary market is disrupted.
- **Liquidity:** depth of the exchange market versus fund-dealing frequency.
- **Price:** exchange price, which can sit at a premium or discount to NAV, versus dealing at NAV.

The ESMA ETF guidelines (2014/937) still apply, including the "UCITS ETF" identifier.
